extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, attorneys subject to USPTO disciplinary rules, OED staff, and other legal professionals interacting with USPTO discipline procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) of a patent practitioner before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on disbarment or disciplinary action in another jurisdiction, including notice, opportunity to respond, limited wind-up recognition, publication, and reinstatement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline basis (37 C.F.R. § 11.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action by a duly constituted authority of a State (e.g., disbarment) can be the basis for imposing reciprocal discipline (exclusion) before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated: exclusion was ordered 'for violating 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. §§ 10.23(c)(5) by being disbarred from practice as an attorney on ethical grounds by a duly constituted authority of the State of Colorado.' The action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific regulatory violation cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(c)(5) as the ethical standard violated (i.e., disbarment in another jurisdiction on ethical grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order identifies violation of these provisions as the legal/regulatory predicate for exclusion; include precise citation when charging or documenting reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to contest and burden of response (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent seeking to contest imposition of exclusion must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice specified: 'Respondent shall file, within 40 days, a response containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the Supreme Court of the State of Colorado would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).' Failure to timely file forfeits contest rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and service procedures (mailing and publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Notice and Order is mailed; if mailing is returned with no forwarding address, service by publication pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(b) and § 11.35(b) is employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from this matter: Notice and Order mailed January 7, 2010; mailing returned 'moved and left no forwarding address'; service by publication published in the Official Gazette on February 16 and 23, 2010. Publication advised Respondent how to obtain a copy by written request to USPTO General Counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's default determination if no response
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent does not file a response, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d) and impose identical discipline (exclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order: 'Respondent has not filed a response... Accordingly, the USPTO Director hereby determines that: 1) there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and 2) exclusion of Respondent from practice before the USPTO is appropriate.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion effective date and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the USPTO is ordered, effective on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (a): 'Respondent is excluded from the practice of patent, trademark, and other non-patent law before the Office, beginning on the date of this Final Order indicated below.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to wind up client matters (30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office for 30 days from the date of the Final Order solely to wind up client business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (b): 'Respondent is granted limited recognition to practice before the Office beginning on the date of this Final Order and expiring thirty (30) days after the date of this Final Order.' This limited recognition is expressly time-limited and for wind-up purposes only.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to wind up matters and withdraw in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40
rubrics_metrics.description: During the period of limited recognition the respondent must wind up all client business before the Office and withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (c) directs compliance: 'Respondent is directed, during the time of his limited recognition to wind up all client business before the Office and to withdraw from employment in all pending proceedings in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 10.40.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on accepting new clients during limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30-day limited recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (d): 'Respondent is directed not to accept any new clients having business before the Office during the 30 days of limited recognition afforded by this Final Order.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish the Final Order and a Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette and make disciplinary decisions available in the OED Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orders (e) and (f): 'the OED Director shall publish this Final Order' and shall publish the specified Notice of Exclusion in the Official Gazette. Disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 during the period of exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (g): 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 while excluded.' (Section 11.58 contains duties of excluded practitioners — adhere to the specific obligations there.)

rubrics_metrics.name: OED notice to other agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and the reasons for it to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public, pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (h) instructs the OED Director to provide these notices in accordance with § 11.59.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order (i): 'Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement.' Follow the procedural and substantive requirements of § 11.60 when seeking reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core attorney ethical duties cited by state disbarment
rubrics_metrics.description: The state disbarment was based on knowingly violating duties including preservation of client property, diligent performance of services, candor to clients, and abiding by legal rules of substance and procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice text: 'Mr. Martin was disbarred by that jurisdiction for knowingly violating his duty to preserve the property of his clients, his duty to diligently perform services on their behalf, his duty to be candid with them during the course of the professional relationship, and his duty to abide by the legal rules of substance and procedure which affect the administration of justice.' These are substantive professional-conduct standards that support reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for action
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59 provide authority for exclusion and related notices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order cites these statutes and regulations as the legal basis: 'This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.24 and 11.59.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service and mailing requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.11 referenced)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be mailed via first-class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the respondent at the address provided under 37 C.F.R. § 11.11; certificate of service documents the mailing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate of Service: 'I certify that the foregoing Final Order ... was mailed first class certified mail, return receipt requested, this day to the Respondent at the following address provided to OED pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11.' Include dates and address used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of Notice and Order on request
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication of the service notice informs the respondent that they may obtain a copy of the Notice and Order by sending a written request to the USPTO General Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service-by-publication language: a published notice 'notifying Respondent that he may obtain a copy of, inter alia, the Notice and Order by sending a written request to the USPTO General Counsel.' Ensure publication includes instructions for obtaining documents.
